market_context: United States; household produce washing and storage.
title: When Should You Wash Fruit: Before Storing or Before Eating?

seo.title: When Should You Wash Fruit?
seo.meta_description: As a general rule, wait to wash fruit until you are ready to prepare or eat it. Storing produce wet can shorten shelf life; if washed early, dry it thoroughly.
seo.search_intent: Know the best time to wash fruit and how to do it safely.

excerpt: For most fruit, it is best to wait and wash just before preparing or eating. University of Minnesota Extension says this helps preserve quality and shelf life. If you wash produce before storage, dry it thoroughly so free moisture does not encourage mold and softening.
content_html:
Washing all produce as soon as groceries come home sounds convenient, but extra surface moisture can shorten the life of delicate fruit. A simple rule is store it dry and wash when you are ready to use it.

What guidance says

University of Minnesota Extension recommends waiting until preparation or eating unless produce is visibly dirty. The FDA recommends washing fresh produce thoroughly under running water before preparing or eating it.

Why wet storage can be a problem

Water trapped around berries, grapes, or other delicate fruit creates a humid surface that favors mold and softening.

How to wash produce

  • Wash hands first.
  • Use cool running water.
  • Rub surfaces gently; use a clean produce brush on firm items.
  • Do not use soap or detergent.
  • Dry with a clean towel if storing after washing.

Wash even fruit you peel

Rinse the outside before cutting because a knife can transfer dirt and microorganisms from peel to flesh.

What about prewashed produce?

If a package says washed and ready to eat, follow its instructions; rewashing is not necessarily useful.

For most fruit: store dry, wash before use, and skip soap.

faq.question: Should I wash strawberries as soon as I buy them?
faq.answer: Usually no. Waiting until eating helps avoid extra moisture that can shorten shelf life.

faq.question: Should I wash an orange if I do not eat the peel?
faq.answer: Yes before cutting or handling it with a knife, so surface contamination is not transferred inward.

faq.question: Can I wash fruit with soap?
faq.answer: No. FDA advises against soap, detergent, and commercial produce washes.
